question: Which medication group is commonly given to treat roundworms by paralyzing them so the body can pass them out?

options.A: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
options.B: Inhaled corticosteroid anti-inflammatories
options.C: Broad-spectrum beta-lactam antibiotics
options.D: Benzimidazoles like albendazole

explanation: Drugs like albendazole and mebendazole mess up the worm's metabolism, paralyzing it so your gut can clear it out easily. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T22#GNS313_U2_T22_h5)

question: When should you choose sterile surgical gloves instead of regular exam gloves?

options.A: When performing a procedure inside a sterile body cavity
options.B: During routine physical checks on unbroken skin
options.C: Whenever touching a patient with an infection
options.D: When cleaning up a blood spill on the floor

explanation: Whenever you enter a sterile space or use sterile instruments, you need sterile gloves to keep bacteria out. You've got this! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h3)

question: Which of the following is a direct surveillance responsibility for a clinical nurse?

options.A: Enforcing federal health policies in the national parliament
options.B: Importing international vaccines for national distribution
options.C: Conducting post-mortem examinations on all deceased patients
options.D: Reporting suspected cases of priority diseases immediately

explanation: Nurses must promptly notify public health authorities when they encounter suspected cases of dangerous or reportable diseases. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h6)

question: Why would a nurse researcher go for a correlational design?

options.A: To randomly assign patients to different hospital diets
options.B: To prove that variable A causes variable B to change
options.C: To test the effectiveness of a brand-new surgical tool
options.D: To explore the relationship between two existing variables

explanation: You got it! Correlation checks how two things relate to each other (like stress and lack of sleep), without claiming one directly causes the other. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T3#GNS224_U1_T3_h5)

question: What does evaluating a menu mean in quality improvement?

options.A: A strict punishment system for kitchen staff who make cooking errors
options.B: A continuous process of gathering feedback and adjusting meals to meet client needs
options.C: A one-time inspection that happens only when the kitchen first opens
options.D: A method to permanently stop changing the food served in the ward

explanation: It's all about checking in regularly, listening to patient feedback, and tweaking the menu so everyone is well-fed and happy. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T005#GNS227_U3_T005_h7)

question: When wearing personal protective equipment (PPE) during an outbreak, what is a common hazard nurses need to watch out for?

options.A: Contaminating oneself while taking off the gear incorrectly
options.B: Causing the laboratory printer to jam during data entry
options.C: Forgetting to check the expiration date on the patient's chart
options.D: Catching a cold from the air conditioning in the isolation room

explanation: You got it! Taking off (doffing) PPE the wrong way is one of the easiest ways healthcare workers accidentally contaminate themselves. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h7)

question: What are the two main parts that make up a patient's overall level of consciousness?

options.A: Speech and memory
options.B: Reflexes and coordination
options.C: Arousal and awareness
options.D: Strength and sensation

explanation: Consciousness is all about being awake (arousal) and being able to interact with your surroundings and thoughts (awareness). Both are essential! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T20#GNS222_U3_T20_h2)

question: When is the best time for a nurse to document that a medication was given?

options.A: While walking down the hallway to the room
options.B: Right before taking the pills out of the drawer
options.C: At the very end of the entire work shift
options.D: Immediately after the patient swallows the drug

explanation: Documenting right away prevents accidental double-dosing and ensures an accurate record of care. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h3)

question: What is your very first nursing action when a patient starts having a tonic-clonic seizure in bed?

options.A: Restrain all four limbs tightly to prevent injury
options.B: Immediately sit the patient upright in a chair
options.C: Open the jaw and insert a padded tongue depressor
options.D: Protect the airway and turn the patient onto their side

explanation: Safety first! Turning them sideways keeps saliva and vomit from blocking their airway. Never force anything into a seizing patient's mouth. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T23#GNS222_U3_T23_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT something a government agency typically does in the food supply chain?

options.A: Managing social safety nets like school feeding programs
options.B: Regulating the import and export of agricultural commodities
options.C: Setting retail prices for every independent restaurant in the country
options.D: Enforcing food safety standards and conducting health inspections

explanation: Governments check food safety and handle imports, but they don't micromanage what individual restaurants charge for a plate of food! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T029#GNS227_U2_T029_h3)

question: A primary health center wants to attract more working fathers to clinics. Which strategy is most effective?

options.A: Stopping all maternal health services to focus only on men
options.B: Introducing flexible clinic hours or dedicated men's health desks
options.C: Banning women from entering the clinic alone
options.D: Punishing men who refuse to attend antenatal visits

explanation: Creating welcoming spaces and flexible schedules accommodates men's work realities and encourages them to participate. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h6)

question: A mother asks which local foods she can give her toddler to prevent iron deficiency. What should you recommend?

options.A: Cassava flakes (garri) soaked in plain cold water
options.B: Pure vegetable oil and polished white rice
options.C: White bread, refined sugar, and bottled juices
options.D: Lean meats, liver, beans, and dark green leafy vegetables

explanation: Foods like liver, beans, and local greens (like ugwu) are fantastic, budget-friendly sources of iron to keep little ones strong and energized. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T005#GNS227_U1_T005_h6)

question: A patient with diabetes keeps sneaking traditional sugary snacks. What is the best first step for the nurse?

options.A: Report the patient to the medical team for non-compliance
options.B: Refuse to provide any further nursing care until they comply
options.C: Remove all personal food items from the bedside table
options.D: Respect their autonomy while calmly explaining the health risks

explanation: You're building great clinical judgment! Instead of policing or scolding, we respect their choice while gently teaching them why health risks matter. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h2)

question: What is a tough ethical situation a home-birth midwife might face during an emergency?

options.A: A client refusing a recommended transfer to a hospital facility
options.B: Deciding which brand of delivery gloves to purchase
options.C: Having too many medical doctors volunteering at a home birth
options.D: Complaining about the weather conditions during labor

explanation: It's a tricky balance! You must respect a patient's choices, but your clinical duty is to keep mom and baby safe when danger arises. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T3#GNS225_U3_T3_h8)

question: A nurse notices that a surgical drain has produced 300 mL of bright red blood in the last hour. What is the most appropriate initial action?

options.A: Strip the tubing vigorously to clear out any remaining blood clots
options.B: Elevate the collection bag above the level of the patient's wound
options.C: Document the normal finding and check the patient again tomorrow
options.D: Notify the surgeon immediately because this suggests active hemorrhage

explanation: A sudden, large volume of bright red drainage indicates heavy bleeding inside the body, which requires urgent medical intervention. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h4)

question: How do opioids cause dangerous breathing slowdowns (respiratory depression) during an overdose?

options.A: By blocking receptors in the brainstem that control breathing
options.B: By physically blocking air from entering the trachea
options.C: By paralyzing the muscles in the hands and arms
options.D: By causing the lung tissue to fill with fluid instantly

explanation: Opioids target the control center in the brainstem, effectively dampening the body's natural urge to breathe. This is why monitoring breathing is always top priority! [learn more](GNS125_U2_T9#GNS125_U2_T9_h3)

question: What is widely known as the biggest challenge facing drug safety systems around the world?

options.A: Underreporting of adverse drug reactions
options.B: Too many digital reporting applications
options.C: Immediate withdrawal of safe medications
options.D: An excess of trained clinical investigators

explanation: Spot on! Many busy clinicians forget or fail to report side effects, meaning most mild or moderate reactions go completely undocumented. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T1#GNS215_U2_T1_h7)

question: What stock rotation rule should be followed when storing sterile supplies?

options.A: Last-in, first-out
options.B: Random selection
options.C: First-in, first-out
options.D: Alphabetical order

explanation: Just like in a pharmacy or supermarket, 'First-In, First-Out' (FIFO) means older stock gets used first so nothing sits on the shelf long enough to expire. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h7)

question: What is the main job of 'moulding' during labour?

options.A: To increase the total volume of brain tissue
options.B: To permanently fuse the cranial sutures early
options.C: To prevent the baby from breathing amniotic fluid
options.D: To reduce the skull dimensions to fit the pelvis

explanation: Moulding is the baby's superpower for birth! The skull bones gently overlap so the head shapes itself to fit easily through the birth canal without harming the brain. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T13#GNS121_U6_T13_h6)

question: What does an electromyography (EMG) test mainly measure?

options.A: Pressure inside joint capsules
options.B: Mineral density inside long bones
options.C: Blood flow through deep leg veins
options.D: Electrical activity within skeletal muscles

explanation: An EMG uses tiny needle electrodes in the muscle to check its electrical signals. It helps doctors figure out if a problem comes from the nerve or the muscle itself. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T4#GNS222_U1_T4_h5)

question: What key cellular sign helps a pathologist identify chronic endometritis under a microscope?

options.A: Complete absence of any immune cells
options.B: The presence of plasma cells in the endometrial stroma
options.C: Enlarged muscle fibers in the outer wall
options.D: An overwhelming number of red blood cells

explanation: While acute infections bring neutrophils, chronic (long-term) endometritis is officially diagnosed by spotting plasma cells hiding out in the tissue lining. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T20#GNS216_U5_T20_h3)

question: At what point in an illness can a patient usually start receiving palliative care?

options.A: Only during the final twenty-four hours of life
options.B: At the time of a serious illness diagnosis
options.C: Only when admitted to a dedicated hospice facility
options.D: After all curative treatments have completely failed

explanation: You don't have to wait until the end! Palliative care is meant to start early alongside other treatments to keep the patient as comfortable as possible. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T2#GNS221_U4_T2_h1)

question: Why does safe motherhood include mental and social well-being alongside physical health?

options.A: Because total health affects a woman's ability to care for herself and her baby
options.B: Because mental health issues only occur after delivery
options.C: Because physical health cannot be measured during pregnancy
options.D: Because social status is the only cause of maternal mortality

explanation: A holistic view of health recognizes that emotional and social support are just as vital as physical care for a mother and her child. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T44#GNS214_U1_T44_h1)

question: When is a therapeutic thoracocentesis performed?

options.A: When trapped fluid causes severe respiratory distress
options.B: When a patient requires daily routine blood tests
options.C: When doctors need to rule out a simple skin rash
options.D: When checking the strength of the heart valves

explanation: Therapeutic drainage is done to physically remove enough fluid to relieve pressure on the lungs and ease breathing. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T17#GNS221_U2_T17_h2)

question: What does disease 'eradication' mean in public health?

options.A: Lowering local cases to an acceptable level
options.B: Eliminating a disease from one specific country
options.C: Permanent reduction to zero of worldwide incidence
options.D: Stopping an outbreak in a single hospital ward

explanation: You've got this! Eradication means the disease is completely wiped out across the entire globe, so we never have to fight it again. Smallpox is a great example! [learn more](GNS313_U1_T16#GNS313_U1_T16_h1)

question: Which low-cost test is commonly used in Nigerian primary health clinics to check for early cervical cell changes?

options.A: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiography
options.B: Visual Inspection with Acetic Acid
options.C: Positron emission tomography scans
options.D: Magnetic resonance imaging scans

explanation: Correct! VIA (Visual Inspection with Acetic Acid) is quick, affordable, and works wonderfully in everyday primary care clinics where high-tech scanners aren't available. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T3#GNS321_U1_T3_h4)

question: How does an RCA team usually investigate an adverse event?

options.A: Blaming the most junior nurse on duty during the shift
options.B: Asking successive layers of 'why' to find deep system weaknesses
options.C: Ignoring past incidents to focus only on the current patient
options.D: Throwing away all existing hospital safety manuals

explanation: By asking 'why' over and over, the team gets past the surface and uncovers the real workflow issues that caused the problem. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h4)

question: A home health registered nurse notices a sudden worsening of a patient's heart failure symptoms. What is the most appropriate immediate action?

options.A: Wait until the scheduled visit next week to document it
options.B: Discharge the patient from home care services immediately
options.C: Report the clinical changes to the primary physician
options.D: Ask the physical therapist to adjust the cardiac medications

explanation: Registered nurses must promptly report significant changes in patient status to the attending doctor to prevent avoidable hospital admissions. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is a key nursing duty right before an upper GI (throat and esophagus) dilation?

options.A: Administering a heavy oral laxative to clear the esophagus
options.B: Ensuring removable dental appliances are taken out
options.C: Instructing the patient to drink large volumes of water
options.D: Placing a heavy weighted blanket over the patient's chest

explanation: False teeth or removable dental plates can easily pop loose and block the airway during throat procedures, so they must always be taken out first. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T19#GNS212_U1_T19_h4)

question: What happens inside a bone when a tumor starts growing in it?

options.A: Normal bone remodeling balance is disrupted, leading to weakened bone integrity
options.B: Calcium is rapidly absorbed back into the matrix, making bones harder
options.C: Bone marrow production shuts down permanently without affecting bone strength
options.D: The bone responds by producing extra thick layers of solid cortical bone

explanation: Tumors mess up the normal building and breaking down process of bones, leaving them fragile. Great job keeping this in mind! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T19#GNS222_U1_T19_h2)

question: What is 'primary non-fulfillment' when talking about medication adherence?

options.A: The patient forgets to take afternoon doses only
options.B: The patient stops taking drugs after feeling better
options.C: The patient never fills or picks up the new prescription
options.D: The patient cuts their pills in half to save money

explanation: Think of it as step one: they leave the clinic with a script, but never actually buy or pick up the medicine. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T3#GNS215_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is the primary tool used in tele-nursing to deliver care?

options.A: Information and communication technologies
options.B: Surgical instruments and sterile trays
options.C: Laboratory reagents and microscopy
options.D: Manual blood pressure cuffs and stethoscopes

explanation: Tele-nursing relies fundamentally on electronic communication tools like phones and computers to reach patients remotely. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h1)

question: How does negative feedback differ from positive feedback?

options.A: Negative feedback speeds up heart rate, while positive feedback slows it down
options.B: Negative feedback only works in the brain, while positive feedback works in the skin
options.C: Negative feedback causes disease, while positive feedback cures it
options.D: Negative feedback reverses a change, while positive feedback amplifies it

explanation: Don't let the names fool you! Negative feedback works to bring levels back down to normal (like cooling down when you're hot), while positive feedback pushes a change further until a task is done (like during childbirth). [learn more](GNS123_U1_T7#GNS123_U1_T7_h2)

question: You are nursing a patient undergoing chemotherapy who has a dangerously low white blood cell count. What is your top priority action?

options.A: Practicing strict hand hygiene and enforcing protective isolation measures
options.B: Encouraging the patient to eat fresh, unwashed raw fruits and salads daily
options.C: Avoiding all vital sign checks to prevent disturbing the resting patient
options.D: Allowing large groups of visitors to visit at any time to boost morale

explanation: When white blood cell counts are down, the body's defense shield is lowered. Rigorous hand hygiene and protective isolation are vital to keep everyday environmental germs away from them. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T14#GNS111_U2_T14_h8)

question: Why can no single agency handle a major disaster completely on its own?

options.A: Government rules forbid any agency from working alone
options.B: Agencies prefer to wait for outside help before starting
options.C: Individual organizations lack any trained leadership staff
options.D: No single agency has all the necessary resources and expertise

explanation: Major emergencies overwhelm the capacity of any single group, making teamwork across various sectors necessary for survival and recovery. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h1)

question: What kind of air pressure do they use inside an operating room to keep outside hallway air from rushing in?

options.A: Neutral pressure
options.B: Positive pressure
options.C: Negative pressure
options.D: Vacuum pressure

explanation: Think of positive air pressure like a gentle wind blowing outward whenever the door opens, keeping the dirty hallway air away from the clean theatre. [learn more](GST114_U2_T13#GST114_U2_T13_h2)

question: What equipment provides the gold standard for sterilizing surgical instruments using moist heat?

options.A: Hot air oven
options.B: Pressure cooker
options.C: Autoclave
options.D: Boiling water bath

explanation: The autoclave uses pressurized steam to achieve temperatures high enough to kill bacterial spores effectively. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h2)

question: Why does diabetes mellitus significantly increase a person's risk for developing CAD?

options.A: Pancreatic failure lowers the overall volume of body fluids
options.B: High blood sugar damages blood vessel linings over time
options.C: Extra sugar in the blood thickens the heart valves directly
options.D: Diabetes forces the kidneys to stop producing red blood cells

explanation: Chronic high blood glucose levels injure the delicate inner lining of arteries, making it much easier for plaque to form. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h3)

question: Apart from bedside clinical work, what is a key role for a community health nurse?

options.A: Purchasing medical equipment for tertiary teaching hospitals
options.B: Financing the construction of primary healthcare centers
options.C: Acting as an educator and facilitator for health programs
options.D: Drafting national health policies in the federal ministry

explanation: You nailed it! Community nurses spend a lot of time teaching families, running workshops, and helping communities organize their own health activities. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T3#GNS124_U4_T3_h6)

question: Where in the body is Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH) originally manufactured?

options.A: The hypothalamus
options.B: The adrenal medulla
options.C: The gonads
options.D: The anterior pituitary

explanation: Correct! Special nerve cells tucked inside the hypothalamus build and release GnRH to kickstart the whole reproductive cascade. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T7#GNS121_U4_T7_h3)

question: What is a major part of making an individual birth preparedness plan with a pregnant woman?

options.A: Identifying emergency transport and travel funds
options.B: Booking a private room at a tertiary hospital
options.C: Planning an elective induction at 37 weeks
options.D: Purchasing expensive formula milk in advance

explanation: Well done! Planning ahead for transport and money cuts out dangerous delays when sudden emergencies pop up. You're thinking like a true public health nurse! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h8)

question: Which nursing action helps thin thick respiratory secretions so they are easier for the patient to cough up?

options.A: Lying the patient flat on their back
options.B: Keeping the room air completely dry
options.C: Encouraging adequate daily fluid intake
options.D: Restricting all drinking water after meals

explanation: Drinking enough water keeps body fluids thin, which naturally loosens thick mucus in the respiratory tract. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T4#GNS212_U2_T4_h7)

question: Why do we stress daily weight monitoring as a crucial self-care habit for heart failure patients?

options.A: It catches fluid retention and worsening heart failure early
options.B: It tells the patient exactly how many calories they burned
options.C: It replaces the need for measuring blood pressure daily
options.D: It measures the thickness of the left ventricular muscle

explanation: Spot on! Scales don't lie. A sudden weight gain over a day or two is often the very first warning sign that fluid is building up, long before severe breathlessness strikes. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T1#GNS223_U1_T1_h7)

question: What is the medical term for trouble swallowing in advanced degenerative diseases?

options.A: Apraxia
options.B: Aphasia
options.C: Dysphagia
options.D: Ataxia

explanation: Dysphagia means difficulty swallowing. Spotting this early helps us protect patients from choking or getting food in their lungs! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h6)

question: What does a Non-Stress Test (NST) actually check for?

options.A: Fetal heart rate changes in response to movement
options.B: The maturity of the fetal lungs before delivery
options.C: The exact amount of protein in maternal urine
options.D: Maternal blood pressure fluctuations over time

explanation: An NST looks at how the baby's heart rate reacts when they move around. A healthy baby's heart rate speeds up a bit with movement—simple and non-invasive! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h4)

question: In rehabilitation terms, how is a 'handicap' different from an 'impairment'?

options.A: An impairment is always caused by poverty
options.B: An impairment cannot be treated by nurses
options.C: A handicap is the social disadvantage resulting from a disability
options.D: A handicap refers strictly to internal organ failure

explanation: Think of an impairment as the physical body change, while a handicap is how that change creates hurdles in everyday social roles and activities. Keep pushing forward! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T17#GNS225_U5_T17_h1)

question: Why must you cross-check delivery notes with actual physical supplies before paying a vendor?

options.A: It guarantees that the supplier will offer a discount on the next order
options.B: It automatically updates the expiration dates of the received medications
options.C: It prevents paying for items that were billed but never actually delivered
options.D: It satisfies the legal requirement for filing annual income taxes

explanation: Always count what's in the box! Checking physical goods against the invoice protects the hospital from paying for items that were left out or short-supplied. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T3#GNS215_U3_T3_h5)

question: What is the normal resting heart rate range for a healthy adult?

options.A: 60 to 100 beats per minute
options.B: 80 to 140 beats per minute
options.C: 40 to 60 beats per minute
options.D: 100 to 120 beats per minute

explanation: You've got this! A healthy adult's heart normally beats between 60 and 100 times per minute while resting. This keeps enough blood flowing to all parts of the body. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h1)

question: What is one of the most important goals of nursing education when it comes to menstrual health?

options.A: Helping clients track their cycle patterns and identify potential red flags
options.B: Prescribing appropriate anti-inflammatory medications for cramps
options.C: Performing internal pelvic examinations to check uterine size
options.D: Diagnosing the underlying hormonal cause of heavy bleeding

explanation: As nurses, one of our greatest superpowers is patient education! Teaching women how to track their cycles and spot danger signs empowers them to take charge of their health. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T4#GNS121_U5_T4_h7)

question: What should you do right after a patient finishes their steam inhalation session?

options.A: Spray the patient's throat with strong antiseptics
options.B: Assist the patient in wiping their mouth and face
options.C: Immediately place the boiling jar into an ice bath
options.D: Seal the dirty water inside the jar for laboratory testing

explanation: Exactly! Gently wiping their face clears away any condensed moisture or medicine residue so it doesn't dry on their skin and cause irritation. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T6#GNS212_U2_T6_h7)

question: At which point in the chain of infection does patient isolation work best?

options.A: Portal of entry
options.B: Susceptible host
options.C: Mode of transmission
options.D: Infectious agent

explanation: Brilliant! By keeping an infected patient apart and limiting contact, isolation blocks the exact pathway germs use to travel from person to person. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h1)

question: What is the very FIRST thing a nurse should do when a patient suddenly gets severe shortness of breath?

options.A: Help the patient sit up and check their oxygen delivery
options.B: Leave the room immediately to find the attending doctor
options.C: Document the exact time the symptoms started
options.D: Have the patient lie flat on their back for rest

explanation: Patient comfort and breathing come first! Always help them sit upright and check their oxygen before you start writing notes or running off. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T10#GNS213_U2_T10_h8)

question: When applying a temporary splint to a suspected fracture, which joints should you include?

options.A: Only the single joint closest to the end of the broken bone
options.B: Only the joint directly below the location of the break
options.C: The joints immediately above and below the fracture site
options.D: Every single joint located throughout the entire injured limb

explanation: Spot on! To truly keep a broken bone stable, you must immobilize the joints right above and right below it. This stops the bone ends from shifting and protects the nearby tissues. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T4#GNS112_U7_T4_h4)

question: The main benefit of assertive communication for patient safety is that it...

options.A: speeds up the hospital discharge process completely
options.B: replaces the need for doctors to write prescriptions
options.C: stops unsafe orders from being carried out blindly
options.D: ensures patients never experience hospital side effects

explanation: An assertive nurse speaks up immediately when a care plan poses a risk to the patient. [learn more](GST321_U7_T5#GST321_U7_T5_h3)

question: What is the best way to help prevent atelectasis in a patient after surgery?

options.A: Restricting fluid intake to prevent fluid overload in the chest
options.B: Administering a strong sleeping pill to ensure total rest
options.C: Encouraging regular deep breathing and incentive spirometry
options.D: Keeping the patient completely flat in bed to rest the lungs

explanation: Spot on! Getting the patient to take deep breaths and use their incentive spirometer pops those little air sacs wide open and keeps the lungs clear. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T12#GNS213_U2_T12_h8)

question: Which diagnostic test is routinely performed for almost every patient who experiences syncope to check for heart rhythm issues?

options.A: Echocardiogram
options.B: Computed tomography scan
options.C: Electrocardiogram
options.D: Electroencephalogram

explanation: An ECG is a standard, rapid test used to spot dangerous heart arrhythmias that could cause fainting. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T16#GNS123_U3_T16_h5)

question: What is the main feature of an urban 'food desert'?

options.A: Excessive government control over neighborhood food prices
options.B: A complete absence of any stores selling edible products
options.C: An abundance of local farms producing fresh vegetables
options.D: A lack of nearby supermarkets offering fresh, affordable food

explanation: A food desert is an area where fresh, healthy food is hard to find, leaving people relying mostly on processed snacks from corner shops. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T021#GNS227_U2_T021_h4)

question: On her third day after delivery, a patient complains that her right calf is painful, swollen, and feels warmer than the left. What is the most important thing you should do?

options.A: Encourage her to walk briskly around the hospital corridor
options.B: Massage the calf firmly to break up any muscle cramps
options.C: Apply an ice pack directly to the painful calf muscle
options.D: Instruct the patient to stay off her feet and notify the physician immediately

explanation: This sounds like a deep vein thrombosis (blood clot). Never massage a suspected clot, as it could break loose and travel to the lungs—always keep the patient resting and call the doctor right away! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h7)

question: According to Piaget, which stage of thinking do teenagers enter?

options.A: Concrete operational stage
options.B: Preoperational stage

question: A patient who received a light sedative for a joint scan is awake and asking to go home. What must you confirm before discharge?

options.A: That all physical pain in the joint has completely disappeared
options.B: That the patient has successfully voided a large amount of radioactive urine
options.C: That the radiologist has already completed the final written diagnostic report
options.D: That the patient has stable vital signs, a clear airway, and a responsible escort home

explanation: Sedatives can mess with a person's reflexes and clear thinking for hours. Always make sure they have stable vitals and a trusted adult to take them home safely. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T5#GNS222_U1_T5_h7)

question: Why is keeping a patient on a continuous heart monitor so crucial during a severe electrolyte or hormone shift?

options.A: Rapid shifts in minerals can trigger dangerous heart rhythms
options.B: Blood pressure cuffs cannot measure pulses during a crisis
options.C: Patients with hormone imbalances always have blocked arteries
options.D: Endocrine organs share direct nerve pathways with heart muscle

explanation: Your heart muscle loves stable electrolytes. When minerals like potassium and calcium fluctuate wildly, the heart's electrical rhythm can become dangerously unstable. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T16#GNS222_U2_T16_h8)

question: Why do hospital policies play a big role in what you are allowed to do during clinicals?

options.A: They dictate what nursing students are legally permitted to perform on patients
options.B: They set the tuition fees for the university nursing department
options.C: They determine the exact colors of the school uniforms
options.D: They write all the final examinations for the nursing council

explanation: Hospitals have strict rules to protect patients and keep student practice within safe, legal boundaries. [learn more](GST321_U8_T5#GST321_U8_T5_h5)

question: A patient sitting in a wheelchair for long hours is most likely to develop pressure sores on which specific area?

options.A: Ischial tuberosities
options.B: Occipital bone
options.C: Bridge of the nose
options.D: Anterior patella

explanation: The ischial tuberosities are simply your sitting bones! When a patient sits for too long, these bones take the heavy brunt of the body weight. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h2)

question: How does a provoked seizure differ from epilepsy?

options.A: Provoked seizures require lifelong anti-seizure medication
options.B: Provoked seizures occur due to a temporary, acute trigger like low blood sugar
options.C: Provoked seizures are always generalized tonic-clonic events
options.D: Provoked seizures only happen during sleep cycles

explanation: A provoked seizure happens because of a temporary stressor on the body, such as high fever or low blood sugar, rather than a chronic brain condition. Great job thinking it through! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T9#GNS222_U4_T9_h1)

question: What is the usual time gap between taking mifepristone and misoprostol?

options.A: Exactly one week apart
options.B: 24 to 48 hours
options.C: Immediately at the same time
options.D: 12 to 14 days apart

explanation: You'll often see 24 to 48 hours prescribed—this gives the first drug enough time to do its job so the second drug can work effectively. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T012#GNS226_U5_T012_h4)

question: What is a key nursing action when a dying patient is experiencing spiritual distress?

options.A: Ignore the comments because physical comfort is the only priority
options.B: Arrange a visit from a spiritual leader who matches the patient's beliefs
options.C: Convince the patient to adopt your own personal religious philosophy
options.D: Administer a sedative medication to calm the patient's anxious mind

explanation: Holistic care means caring for the spirit too. Connecting them with someone who shares their faith brings great peace. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T2#GNS221_U4_T2_h4)

question: Why is vitamin K given as an injection to a newborn baby?

options.A: To treat neonatal jaundice caused by blood incompatibility
options.B: To prevent bleeding disorders due to immature clotting factors
options.C: To stimulate spontaneous crying and lung expansion
options.D: To protect the infant against bacterial eye infections

explanation: You got it! A newborn's tummy is sterile and doesn't make vitamin K yet, so this shot protects them from dangerous bleeding. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T11#GNS225_U3_T11_h6)

question: When should you usually give a patient their pain medication before a scheduled dressing change?

options.A: Right after you finish the dressing change
options.B: About 30 minutes before the procedure
options.C: Only if the patient starts crying
options.D: Two hours before so it wears off

explanation: Giving pain meds about half an hour early gives the drug time to kick in right when you start cleaning sensitive tissue. Patient comfort is key! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h4)

question: Which symptom during the final months of pregnancy strongly points to placenta previa?

options.A: High fever with foul-smelling amniotic fluid
options.B: Sudden swelling of the feet only
options.C: Painless bright red vaginal bleeding
options.D: Severe painful contractions with a rigid belly

explanation: Well done! Placenta previa happens when the placenta covers the cervix, which typically causes sudden, painless, bright red bleeding. You are mastering your obstetric signs! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h2)

question: What is the main reason nurses use portable monitors in the hospital?

options.A: To track vital signs while a patient is moving
options.B: To permanently store a patient's entire medical history
options.C: To deliver intravenous medications automatically
options.D: To replace all stationary equipment in the intensive care unit

explanation: Portable monitors are lifesavers when patients are walking around or being moved between wards. They let us keep a close eye on vitals on the go! [learn more](GNS212_U4_T10#GNS212_U4_T10_h1)

question: Which set of clinical signs points directly to neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS)?

options.A: High fever, extreme muscle rigidity, and unstable vitals
options.B: Uncontrolled euphoria and excessive talkativeness
options.C: Hyperactive bowel sounds and sudden weight loss
options.D: Slurred speech, itchy skin rash, and low fever

explanation: Think of NMS as a dangerous fire in the body: extremely high fever, muscles stiff as boards (lead-pipe rigidity), and wild swings in blood pressure and heart rate. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T6#GNS223_U6_T6_h7)

question: Why is keeping blood pressure under control so important for preventing strokes?

options.A: High blood pressure weakens cerebral vessels and increases stroke risk
options.B: Blood pressure readings tell us if a brain tumor is growing
options.C: Hypertension directly destroys peripheral nerve endings in the feet
options.D: Low blood pressure causes immediate brain cell regeneration

explanation: High blood pressure puts extra strain on the blood vessels feeding the brain, making them much more likely to burst or block. Controlling it saves lives! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T24#GNS222_U3_T24_h2)

question: Why do nurses check kidney function (like serum creatinine) before starting certain first-line ARVs?

options.A: Drugs like tenofovir can affect renal function and require safe dosing
options.B: It proves whether the patient has active tuberculosis infection
options.C: Good kidney function guarantees the patient will never miss a dose
options.D: Kidney tests tell the nurse how many CD4 cells the patient has left

explanation: You're right! Some drugs like Tenofovir can put stress on the kidneys, so checking baseline labs ensures the medication is completely safe for that patient's body. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T4#GNS216_U6_T4_h5)
